implementation_plan.title: xxHash64 byte-reading and mixing primitives
implementation_plan.goal: Port xxh_is_little_endian, xxh_read_le64/_align, xxh_swap32, xxh_read32, xxh_get_32bits, xxh_read_le32_align, xxh64_round, xxh64_merge_round, xxh64_avalanche, xxh64_finalize, xxh64_get64bits, using wrapping_* arithmetic to match C's silent uint64_t/uint32_t wraparound. Pure functions, no Cset<T> state.
steps_part_a: Implement xxh_is_little_endian via 1u32.to_ne_bytes()[0] == 1.
Implement xxh_read_le64 (unsafe 8-byte forward read + shift/OR) and xxh_read_le64_align (thin wrapper) and xxh_get64bits (delegates to xxh_read_le64_align).
Implement xxh_swap32 and xxh_read32 (unsafe 4-byte read).
Implement xxh64_round and xxh64_merge_round with wrapping_add/wrapping_mul/rotate_left(31), matching C exactly.
Implement xxh_get_32bits/xxh_read_le32_align dispatching on xxh_is_little_endian() at runtime (raw read vs swapped read).
Implement xxh64_avalanche (wrapping_mul + xor-shift chain).
Implement xxh64_finalize (len &= 31; 8-byte loop via xxh_get64bits/xxh64_round; 4-byte via xxh_get_32bits; 1-byte tail loop; final xxh64_avalanche), confining unsafe pointer advances to this fn.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] from test_xxh_is_little_endian_matches_platform and implement its assertion.

Remove #[ignore] from test_xxh64_known_answer_empty_input/_long_input once xxh64/xxh64_h exist (M2) so the >32-byte block-mixing path and the finalize tail path are both exercised; may stage KAT values here but finalize activation happens after M2.

implementation_plan.title: xxh64 / xxh64_h top-level hash and cset hash callbacks
implementation_plan.goal: Implement xxh64_endian_align, xxh64_endian_align_h (independently-seeded variants), xxh64, xxh64_h, and cset_hash1_callback/cset_hash2_callback (hash2 forced odd via | 1) using CSET_DEFAULT_SEED. Deterministic and self-consistent with M1 primitives.
steps_part_a: Implement xxh64_endian_align: len>=32 block-mixing loop (v1..v4 seeded seed+PRIME64_1+PRIME64_2 / seed+PRIME64_2 / seed+0 / seed-PRIME64_1) else seed+PRIME64_5, then += len, then xxh64_finalize.
Implement xxh64_endian_align_h with its distinct v2/v3 seeding (seed-PRIME64_2 / seed+PRIME64_3) and else-branch += PRIME64_1, preserving the asymmetry vs xxh64_endian_align.
Implement xxh64(input: *const u8, len, seed) delegating to xxh64_endian_align after an unsafe raw-pointer-to-byte-slice view (handle input possibly null/len 0 as C does).
Implement xxh64_h delegating to xxh64_endian_align_h.
Implement cset_hash1_callback = xxh64(memptr, size, CSET_DEFAULT_SEED); cset_hash2_callback = xxh64_h(...) | 1.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] and finish test_xxh64_known_answer_empty_input/_long_input (KAT / self-consistency assertions).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_cset_hash2_callback_always_odd (assert result & 1 == 1 across several inputs).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_hash1_and_hash2_are_independent (assert hash1 != hash2 for representative inputs).

implementation_plan.goal: Implement Cset::new() allocating CSET_INITIAL_CAP zero-initialized buckets (pi=0), seed=CSET_DEFAULT_SEED, max_load_factor=0.7, min_load_factor=0.2, bucket_size=0, compare=None, empty temp_buckets. Implement get/set accessors and empty()/tombstone() predicates.
steps_part_a: Implement Cset::new(): Vec<CsetValue<T>> of length CSET_INITIAL_CAP each { pi: 0, elem: <needs no real value until written -- build without requiring T: Default, e.g. via a placeholder-free construction path that only needs `pi` set for capacity bookkeeping> }; set defaults per goal.
Implement get_size/set_size, get_seed/set_seed, get_max_load_factor/set_max_load_factor, get_min_load_factor/set_min_load_factor as direct field accessors.
Implement get_buckets/get_buckets_ref/get_temp_buckets_ref returning references to the Vec fields.
Implement size() (bucket_size as i32) and capacity() (buckets.len() as i32).

Implement empty()/tombstone() per the scaffold's no-index pub signatures, plus private index-taking helpers (empty_at(&self, i)/tombstone_at(&self, i)) used internally by add/remove/contains/resize/iter in later milestones.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] and implement test_new_default_state: Cset::<i32>::new() has size()==0 and capacity()==CSET_INITIAL_CAP as i32.
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_accessor_round_trip: set_seed/get_seed, set_max_load_factor/get_max_load_factor, set_min_load_factor/get_min_load_factor round-trip correctly.

implementation_plan.title: add / contains with default byte-equality and probing
implementation_plan.goal: Implement double-hashing probe (index = (h1 + i*h2) % cap) using M2 hash callbacks and default raw-byte equality (size_of::<T>()-based) when no comparator is set. Implement add() with duplicate no-op semantics and first-empty-or-tombstone insertion (preserving the exact early-break subtlety), and contains() with tombstone-skipping probe.
steps_part_a: Add private helper(s) for h1/h2 hashing of a &T via its raw-byte representation (size_of::<T>()) using cset_hash1_callback/cset_hash2_callback and self.seed, plus a double_hash_index(h1, h2, i, cap) helper.
Add a private default-equality helper: self.compare.map_or(byte-equality, |f| f(a, b)), where byte-equality compares the raw byte reprs of two &T values via size_of::<T>().

Implement Cset::add(&mut self, value: T) -> i32: pre-insert load-factor check (bucket_size/cap >= max_load_factor triggers a resize, wired as a no-op stub call until M5 lands resize logic), then probe using h1/h2, breaking unconditionally at the first empty-or-tombstone slot (not scanning the whole table for a later duplicate), checking equality against occupied slots visited before that break; on no match, write value+pi=iteration into the found slot and bucket_size += 1; return self.bucket_size as i32 (documented assumption per analysis.md, no C return value exists to consult).
Implement Cset::contains(&mut self, value: &T) -> bool: probe up to cap iterations, skip tombstones, stop at first empty slot or match.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] and implement test_add_duplicate_noop (README: add(1); add(2); add(2) dup -> size unaffected by the duplicate).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_contains_true_false (README: add 34/25/56; contains(34)==true; contains(100)==false).
Stage (but leave #[ignore]'d until M5) test_resize_on_load_factor since full resize semantics land in M5.

implementation_plan.title: remove, tombstones, and load-factor-triggered resize
implementation_plan.goal: Implement remove() marking the found slot's pi=-1 and decrementing bucket_size (no-op if not found). Implement the resize check in add() and resize() itself: rehash all live elements into temp_buckets (dropping tombstones), then swap buckets<->temp_buckets. capacity() reflects the doubled size after a resize.
steps_part_a: Implement Cset::remove(&mut self, value: T) -> i32: probe (same h1/h2 sequence as add/contains), skip tombstones, stop at first empty slot or cap exhaustion; on match set pi=-1 and bucket_size -= 1; return self.bucket_size as i32 (consistent with add's return convention).

Implement the private resize(&mut self, new_cap: usize) helper: build temp_buckets of new_cap zeroed slots, walk current buckets in order, re-add every live (non-empty, non-tombstone) element's elem into temp_buckets via the same add-style probe logic (dropping tombstones by omission), then reset bucket_size accordingly and swap self.buckets with self.temp_buckets (mem::swap or assignment), leaving temp_buckets empty/dropped.
Wire the load-factor check inside Cset::add (from M4) to actually call resize(cap * 2) when bucket_size as f64 / cap as f64 >= max_load_factor, before performing the insert probe.
Implement Cset::clear(&mut self): replace buckets with a fresh CSET_INITIAL_CAP zeroed Vec (old Vec dropped automatically), reset bucket_size = 0.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] and implement test_remove_then_size_zero (README: add(34); assert size==1; remove(34); assert size==0).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_remove_missing_is_noop (remove a value never added; size unchanged).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_clear_resets_size (README: add 34/25/56; clear(); assert size==0).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_resize_on_load_factor (add enough elements to cross the 0.7 load factor; assert capacity() has doubled from CSET_INITIAL_CAP).

implementation_plan.title: clear, index, and iter (bucket-order materialization)
implementation_plan.goal: Implement clear() (already landed in M5; re-verify), index(&self, index) returning the element at a bucket slot, and iter(&mut self) walking buckets in array order, skipping empty/tombstone slots, collecting exactly the live elements into a Vec<T> (bucket order), matching the C iterator's done()/next() termination bound (current_count >= size()).
steps_part_a: Implement Cset::index(&self, index: usize) -> T returning (a clone of) the element at that bucket slot; test instantiations are expected to use Copy types (i32/char) per analysis.md, so clone/copy is safe without a declared T: Clone bound conflict.

Implement Cset::iter(&mut self) -> Vec<T>: walk buckets 0..capacity() in order, skip pi==0 (empty) and pi==-1 (tombstone) slots, push a clone of each live elem, stopping once collected.len() >= self.size() (mirrors the C iterator's current_count >= size() bound) -- though a full single pass naturally terminates at the same point since bucket_size counts exactly the live slots.
steps_part_b: Remove #[ignore] and implement test_iterator_yields_all_elements: add several elements, call iter(), and assert the resulting Vec<T>, compared as a multiset/sorted collection (not insertion order), matches the expected elements exactly.

implementation_plan.title: Custom comparator dispatch
implementation_plan.goal: Implement set_comparator(&mut self, compare) storing the function pointer, and make add/remove/contains use self.compare when Some(...) instead of the default byte-equality fallback from M4, so two distinct values considered equal by the comparator are treated as one for dedup, removal, and membership.
steps_part_a: Implement Cset::set_comparator(&mut self, compare: fn(&T, &T) -> bool): self.compare = Some(compare).
Confirm/adjust the private equality helper (added in M4) is the single dispatch point used by add/remove/contains, so no duplicate equality logic exists to fall out of sync.
steps_part_b: Implement the Node{x,y} fixture and node_comparator(a,b) => a.x == b.x (already stubbed in the tests module).

Remove #[ignore] and implement test_custom_comparator_dedup_by_field mirroring the README Node example: set_comparator(node_comparator); add(Node{4,5}); add(Node{4,4}) is a dedup no-op (size stays 1); add(Node{1,2}) grows size to 2; remove(Node{1,45}) removes by x==1 (size back to 1).

implementation_plan.title: Set algebra: intersect, union, is_disjoint, difference
implementation_plan.goal: Implement intersect(&mut self, first, second) (occupied elements of first that are in second, added into self without clearing self first), union(&mut self, first, second) (all occupied elements of first then second, added into self), is_disjoint(&mut self, other) (true unless some occupied element of self is contained in other, early-exiting on the first shared element), and difference(&mut self, first, second) (occupied elements of first not contained in second), all built on top of add/contains from M4/M7.
steps_part_a: Implement Cset::intersect(&mut self, first: &Self, second: &Self): iterate first's occupied bucket slots (skip empty/tombstone), test membership via second.contains(...) (requires a &mut on second, or a helper that borrows mutably as contains requires -- resolve via interior probe logic without violating borrow rules, e.g. by re-deriving containment via a shared-ref-safe probe path), and self.add(elem) on each match. Do not clear self first.
Implement Cset::union(&mut self, first: &Self, second: &Self): self.add every occupied element of first, then every occupied element of second.
Implement Cset::is_disjoint(&mut self, other: &Self) -> bool: iterate self's occupied elements, testing containment in other; return false and stop at first shared element found, else true.
Implement Cset::difference(&mut self, first: &Self, second: &Self): self.add every occupied element of first that is not contained in second.

Remove #[ignore] and implement test_union_sizes (README: union sizes 5 then 6 after adding a new element to b).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_is_disjoint (two non-overlapping sets are disjoint; adding a shared element makes them not disjoint).
Remove #[ignore] and implement test_difference (elements of a not present in b).
